messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated 5xx rate from EU edge for api.redwood.com (detected by uptime-checker). Error signature: TLS handshake failures + Cloudflare 520/524. Paging Dave (oncall).

Dave (oncall): Ack. I'm looking. Can folks post a quick curl from eu-west and us-east?

Alice S (infra): From my laptop in eu-west-1: 
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.com/health
* Connected to api.redwood.com (172.65.24.10) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate verify failed
* SSL_connect returned=1 errno=0 state=error: certificate verify failed
* Closing connection 0
```

Carla M: Seeing the same from Canary in Frankfurt. Cloudflare edge returns `524` intermittently, and when it's not 5xx we get TLS handshake errors.

Ben K: Checked Cloudflare status page — they have a partial incident flagged for "edge TLS certificate validation" in EU (weirdly intermittent). Link: https://status.cloudflare.com/incident/xxxx (internal note: copy of external).

Eve - Support: Support queue getting ~12 new complaints in last 10m: customers report "cannot connect" and SDKs failing during handshake. High-value customer REX-31 flagged.

Dave (oncall): Triage plan: 1) confirm scope (regions + prefixes) 2) attempt short-term mitigation (route critical traffic around affected edges) 3) gather impacted customers for comms.

ops-bot: Running diag collection (dig, traceroute, certinfo). Will paste results in thread.

ops-bot: 
```
$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.com A +short
172.65.24.10
172.65.24.11
$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.com NS +short
ours-ns-1.example.net.
ours-ns-2.example.net.
```

Alice S (infra): Quick cert check from multiple regions: origin cert on our LB is Let's Encrypt R3, expires in 2026-09. However Cloudflare is presenting an edge cert (as expected). Some edges show a cert chain mismatch: Cloudflare->edge cert signed by unknown intermediate? Attached excerpt: `verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate`

Carla M: I can correlate IP prefixes: affected edges are 172.65.24.x and 198.41.200.x — mostly EU/EMEA. US looks OK.

Ben K: Cloudflare engineering notes this looks like an upstream OCSP/CA validation glitch combined with our custom SNI header. They asked if we're setting a custom `Host:`/SNI that might no longer match any active zone cert after a recent routing change. Did we change any hostname config in last 24h?

Alice S (infra): Not on our side intentionally. But we did deploy a change yesterday to the internal proxy that adds `x-forwarded-host` rewriting for canary. I'll roll that back on canary first.

Dave (oncall): Rollback canary now, please. If that improves, we'll schedule rollback to prod rolling windows.

Alice S (infra): Rolling back proxy canary: `kubectl -n infra rollout undo deployment/proxy-canary --to-revision=3`

Alice S (infra): Done on canary. Monitoring...

ops-bot: Canary curl after rollback: 
```
$ curl -v https://canary.api.redwood.com/health
* Connected to 172.65.24.10 port 443
* TLS handshake completed successfully
* HTTP/2 200
```

Dave (oncall): Canary looks good. That strongly suggests our recent header rewrite interacted poorly with Cloudflare edge cert validation in some regions.

Ben K: For mitigation we should: A) rollback prod proxy rewrite in controlled fashion B) open emergency ticket with Cloudflare (we already have a P1 channel) C) prepare DNS fallback if Cloudflare continues to be flaky for critical customers.

Carla M: I'll prepare a short TTL override to expedite any DNS changes: `dnsctl set-ttl api.redwood.com 60 --zone redwood` (hold until we need it).

Eve - Support: I'll ping REX-31 with interim status: we identified TLS handshake issues at Cloudflare edges; rolling back canary change improved canary. ETA for wider rollback 15-30m.

Ben K: I'm taking over the on-call after Dave — handing off context. Dave, anything else to add?

Dave (oncall): Handing off to Ben K. Key points: 1) Impact: EU customers, TLS handshakes + 5xx 2) Cause likely interaction between our SNI/Host rewrite and Cloudflare edge cert validation 3) Canary rollback fixed canary 4) Mitigations: prod rollback, Cloudflare escalated. I will remain available.

Ben K: Thanks. Executing prod rollback in waves (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with 2m observation windows.

ops-bot: Deploy command: `kubectl -n infra rollout undo deployment/proxy --to-revision=4 --record`

Carla M: Rolling at 10%...

Carla M: 10% -> 2m. Monitoring health and handshake counts.

Carla M: 10% looks good; handshake errors dropped 90% for those hosts. Proceeding to 50%.

Ben K: 50% -> OK. Proceed to 100%.

Carla M: 100% rollback completed. Post-rollback metrics: EU TLS handshake failure rate back to baseline, 5xx rate normalized.

Eve - Support: Pushed update to affected customers: issue mitigated via rollback; we are coordinating with Cloudflare to understand root cause and prevent recurrence.

Ben K: Opening follow-up actions: 1) postmortem with Cloudflare ticket ID + timeline 2) adjust PR checklist to flag SNI/Host header changes and add region canary gating 3) run synthetic cert validation tests from multiple edges during deploys.

Dave (oncall): Marking incident resolved for paging. I'll update incident board and set oncall follow-up chat for 30m postmortem. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident auto-closed (duration ~37m). Summary: transient Cloudflare edge TLS validation issue amplified by internal SNI/header rewrite. Mitigated by canary -> full rollback. Ticket filed with Cloudflare for RCA.
